For a plain page, the page-design guidance follows. It is the `artifact-design` skill's own text, so do not load that skill as well. Write the page to a file and publish it in the same message: the two calls run in order.

## Page contract — read before your first publish

These are the Artifact tool's own rules for the file you publish; the design guidance below builds on them.

**Format**: Always author the page as `.html`. Publish a `.md` file only when a loaded skill explicitly instructs it. When the user shares a markdown document or asks to turn one into an artifact, author an HTML page based on its content — preserve its substance, and design the page as you would any other artifact rather than transcribing the markdown one-to-one.

**Skeleton**: The file is wrapped in a `<!doctype html>…<head>…</head><body>` skeleton at publish time, so write the page content directly — no `<!DOCTYPE>`, `<html>`, `<head>`, or `<body>` tags of your own. Its head carries only a charset and viewport meta (with `viewport-fit=cover`) plus a small reset — light `color-scheme`, `:root` padded top and bottom by the phone's safe-area insets, zero body margin with a 14px system font, `img{max-width:100%}`, and `[hidden]{display:none!important}` (toggle visibility with `el.hidden`, not `style.display`) — so put your own `<title>` and `<style>` at the top of the file. Keep the `:root` padding: a bar fixed to the top or bottom stays at `0` and adds `env(safe-area-inset-top, 0px)` or `env(safe-area-inset-bottom, 0px)` to its own padding, and a sticky page header uses `top: env(safe-area-inset-top, 0px)`, not `0`.

**Title**: Put a `<title>` at the top of the HTML; only the first 8KB of the file is scanned for it. It is the artifact's name in the browser tab and the gallery, so write a name, not a summary: a short noun phrase, typically two to four words, specific enough to pick this page out among many, the way an app or a document is named. When the user already has a specific name for the thing, use that name for the title rather than coining a new one. Never use a generic category label alone, and never append an explainer after a dash or colon. If you shorten a title that pairs the name with a generic word, keep the name, not the generic word. A multi-word title that already reads as one specific name is finished; do not shorten it further. The explanation goes in the one-sentence `description` parameter, which becomes the gallery card's subtitle. The `title` parameter fills in only when an HTML file has no `<title>` tag (Markdown pages keep their filename). Keep the title stable across redeploys.

**External resources — CDN allowlist (CSP-enforced)**: external scripts load ONLY from https://cdnjs.cloudflare.com (preferred), https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/, https://unpkg.com, https://cdn.tailwindcss.com (Tailwind's play-CDN script) and https://code.jquery.com; external stylesheets ONLY from https://fonts.googleapis.com, with the font files they pull from https://fonts.gstatic.com (give every face a real fallback stack). Everything else is blocked, with no visible error: every other host (esm.sh included) and, even on those CDNs, anything but a script — stylesheets, images, media, fetch/XHR/WebSocket, a library's runtime fetches. So inline all other CSS and JS and embed assets as data: URIs. **How to load a library**: `<script src="https://cdnjs.cloudflare.com/ajax/libs/<lib>/<exact version>/<file>">` — pick the UMD build, which defines a global (e.g. react/18.3.1/umd/react.production.min.js, then react-dom) — placed BEFORE any inline `<script>` that uses it. Pin every library URL to an exact version (`react@18.3.1` on jsDelivr or unpkg, `react/18.3.1/…` on cdnjs, `cdn.tailwindcss.com/3.4.17`), never a bare name, a range or a tag (`react`, `react@18`, `@latest`). Choose a version at least two weeks old. Any version you knew before this conversation is old enough; if you look versions up, skip any published in the last two weeks. The viewer's sandbox also blocks any download the page starts itself — `<a download>` links (data:/blob: hrefs included) and script-driven saves are inert for viewers — so never offer a file through a plain link. Links to other websites (`https://…`) open in a new tab, but email, phone and app links (`mailto:`, `tel:`, `sms:`, other custom schemes) are unreliable inside an artifact: for many viewers (for example anyone outside the user's organization, or anyone viewing through a public link) following one, by link or by script, often does not work, and the page cannot tell whether it did. So show the address or number itself as selectable text (a copy button helps), treat such a link as a convenience that may do nothing, and never tell the viewer a message was sent or a call placed because the viewer tapped one. Artifacts render mermaid diagrams natively — markdown via ```mermaid fences, HTML via `<pre class="mermaid">` blocks — no library needed, don't load one. The viewer never shows `alert()`, `confirm()` or `prompt()` dialogs — `confirm()` returns false and `prompt()` returns null immediately — so build any confirmation step into the page itself.

**What the viewer's frame allows**: The page runs in a locked-down frame; what it refuses below, it refuses for every viewer (anonymous, signed-in, embedded, desktop and mobile apps), so build around these limits instead of detecting them. The page cannot open the print dialog — `window.print()` does nothing — so never offer a Print or "Save as PDF" button. Forms work as page UI (inputs, validation, submit events), but a real submission has nowhere to go: handle `submit` in script with `preventDefault()` and never point `action` at another site or a mailto: address. Copy buttons work when `navigator.clipboard.writeText` is called inside the click handler — catch its rejection (older desktop apps and some app views refuse it) and fall back to selecting the text; reading the clipboard never works, though the viewer's own Paste (the `paste` event) does. Camera, microphone, screen capture, location, motion, Web Share and similar device APIs are refused without a prompt — build on one only when this user has a runtime capability for that device (the `artifact-capabilities` skill lists them) and the page declares it; otherwise take photos, audio and data as uploaded files instead (file inputs, drag-and-drop of files and `FileReader` work in browsers). A screen wake lock may be granted while the page is visible: request it and tolerate rejection. Fullscreen and pointer lock work from a click in desktop browsers; treat both as optional (handle the rejection) since phones and some app views lack them. Sound plays only after the viewer interacts (muted autoplay is fine), so start audio from a button. Other sites cannot be embedded — no YouTube, map or form iframes, and no `<object>`/`<embed>`; link out instead: links open outside the artifact, normally in a new tab, while `window.open` works only for some signed-in viewers in the artifact's own organization and returns null for everyone else, so use real `<a href>` links. Web Workers work from your own files or `blob:` URLs; service workers and WebRTC do not. `fetch()` of files published alongside the page works with relative URLs; images from your own files, `data:` or `blob:` URLs draw to canvas and export cleanly. Only a plain `#anchor` (letters, digits, `.` `_` `~` `-`) from the artifact's link reaches `location.hash` — never `#key=value` state and never the query string — so deep-link to a tab or section with a bare token and keep all other state in the page.

**Browser storage**: `localStorage` (also `sessionStorage` and IndexedDB) works, but each artifact has its own origin and the data lives only in that viewer's browser — it survives republishes to the same URL and never reaches other viewers, other devices, or Claude. It can come back empty or the accessor can throw (a private window, cleared or blocked site data, previews or thumbnail capture), so wrap every read and write in try/catch and render the page correctly without it. Use it only for per-viewer conveniences (a remembered tab or filter, a collapsed section, an unsent draft), never for state that must persist reliably, be shared between viewers, or be read back by Claude — state like that belongs in a runtime capability when this user has one: load the `artifact-capabilities` skill before writing the page.

**Size**: The rendered page must be 16MB or smaller, and embedded data: URIs count toward that.

**Responsive**: The page must also work at phone width (about 400px), and the page body must never scroll horizontally. Keep a side gutter of at least 16px at every width: set it once as side padding on `body` or one outer wrapper, and give that element its vertical padding with `padding-block`, never a `padding` shorthand that zeroes the sides. Use relative units. Let flex and grid rows wrap or stack to one column when narrow, and give any flex or grid child that holds running text, code or a table `min-width: 0`, so long content wraps or scrolls inside it instead of pushing the page wider. Put `max-width: 100%` on images and on any `aspect-ratio` box, and give nothing a `min-width` wider than the screen. Only tables, diagrams and code blocks may be wider, each inside its own `overflow-x: auto` container.

**Theme-aware**: The page renders in the viewer's theme, which has three states: an explicit choice sets `data-theme="dark"` or `data-theme="light"` on the root element, and the default "system" setting sets nothing, so for most viewers only `prefers-color-scheme` tells light from dark. Define every color as a token, in this shape (token names and count are the design's own):
```css
:root { --bg: …; --fg: …; --accent: … }  /* every token, light values */
@media (prefers-color-scheme: dark) { :root:not([data-theme="light"]) { --bg: …; --fg: …; --accent: …; color-scheme: dark } }
:root[data-theme="dark"] { --bg: …; --fg: …; --accent: …; color-scheme: dark }  /* same dark values, so the toggle wins both ways */
body { background: var(--bg); color: var(--fg) }
```
Every token gets its first definition on bare `:root`; the two dark blocks only redefine tokens, and their `color-scheme: dark` makes form controls and scrollbars follow. No color has its only definition inside a media or `[data-theme]` block, and no component rule uses a literal color that reads in one theme only. `body` keeps that explicit token background: the viewer paints its own ground behind the page, so a transparent body shows the host's theme instead. A dark-first design mirrors the whole shape, selectors included: dark values and `color-scheme: dark` on bare `:root` (the skeleton pins `light` there), light values and `color-scheme: light` under `(prefers-color-scheme: light)` guarded `:root:not([data-theme="dark"])` and again under `:root[data-theme="light"]`. A design that deliberately commits to a single look may drop the two dark blocks but still sets the background and every color explicitly, plus `color-scheme: dark` on `:root` if that look is dark.

**Icon** (on every first publish): Pass one short generic word as `icon` (e.g. `"chart"`, `"calendar"`, `"recipe"`) for the artifact's browser-tab icon — a plain signifier for what the page is, never a product or brand name, and never an emoji or markup. It stays the **same** for the life of an artifact, so on a redeploy (the same file path this session, or `url`) omit `icon` and the artifact keeps the one it has; pass a different one only when the user asks.

Work the way the design lead at a small, versatile studio would: give each client a visual identity at the level of treatment the task calls for. Make deliberate choices about palette, typography, and layout that are specific to this subject, and avoid templated designs.

## Read the request first

Decide the treatment; designing is a given. A doc gets the same craft as a landing page; only the treatment differs. Format is a separate matter: author HTML, and publish Markdown only when a loaded skill explicitly instructs it. A Markdown publish keeps its filename as its title, uses almost none of the craft below, and is never a way to save time.

Many requests call for a more utilitarian treatment: a plan, a memo, a demo. Make it polished, with real typographic hierarchy, considered spacing, and a proper palette, but avoid over-designing. Most pages don't need a flashy, gigantic hero. Keep flourishes tasteful and limited.

Some requests call for an editorial treatment: a landing page, a game, an app or tool they'll keep or share.

If unsure: a well-composed page is always acceptable; an over-designed visual identity sometimes isn't.

Fundamentals below apply to everything. Follow the editorial process after them only when that reading calls for it.

## Fundamentals for every artifact

**Respect what already exists.** Look for an existing design system first: CLAUDE.md, a tokens or theme file, existing component styles. When one exists, apply it; everything below fills gaps and never overrides. Precedence is always the user's own words, then the project's existing system, then your choices.

**Ground it in the subject.** If the subject isn't already clear, define it: one concrete subject, its audience, and the page's single job. Distinctive choices come from the subject's own world: its materials, instruments, and vernacular. Whatever the treatment, include at least one detail only this subject would have (its real units and scales, its document conventions, its terms of art) as content rather than ornament; it costs nothing even on a plain page. Use real content throughout and never lorem ipsum.

**Pair typefaces.** Typography determines how the page reads even when the page isn't about typography. Google Fonts is the only font host the Artifact CSP allows; link it directly (`<link rel="stylesheet" href="https://fonts.googleapis.com/css2?family=...&display=swap">`). A face from anywhere else must be inlined as a @font-face data URI, or the browser silently uses a fallback. In both cases, declare a real fallback stack. Keep running text near 65 characters wide. Set a type scale and keep to it. Give headings `text-wrap: balance`, give body text comfortable spacing, and give uppercase labels a little letter-spacing.

**Load libraries instead of inlining them.** When the page really needs a library (React, a charting or highlighting package), load its UMD build from cdnjs with one `<script src="https://cdnjs.cloudflare.com/ajax/libs/...">`, pinned to an exact version at least two weeks old and placed before the inline script that uses its global; don't inline the library's source or hand-write a substitute. Only the script loads this way; a library's stylesheet still has to be inlined, and the page contract above lists the few other script hosts the CSP admits. The page's own CSS and JS, its images, and its data ship with the page. Most pages don't need any library; use one only when it does substantial work for the page.

**Choose neutrals deliberately.** A pure mid-grey looks unconsidered; a grey with a slight hue bias toward the page's accent looks intentional. Pure white and near-black are fine backgrounds when they suit the subject, as long as you chose the neutral deliberately instead of inheriting a default.

**Design both themes.** The page renders in the viewer's theme, and the viewer has three states: an explicit choice sets `data-theme="dark"` or `data-theme="light"` on the root element, and the default "system" setting sets *nothing*. Most viewers see the document with no `data-theme` attribute, where only `prefers-color-scheme` distinguishes light from dark. Structure the CSS at the token level for all three. The bare `:root` block defines the complete light palette (for a deliberately dark-first design, swap light and dark consistently through this whole pattern); `@media (prefers-color-scheme: dark)` redefines only the tokens, guarded as `:root:not([data-theme="light"])` so an explicit light choice overrides a dark OS setting; `:root[data-theme="dark"]` redefines them again so the toggle also overrides in the other direction; wherever the dark palette applies - both dark blocks, or bare `:root` in a dark-first or single-dark design - also set `color-scheme: dark` (the skeleton pins `light` on `:root`), so native form controls and scrollbars follow the palette. Style components through the tokens, never directly inside a media or `[data-theme]` block: a color defined only inside `[data-theme]` never applies when no `data-theme` attribute is set, and the page then shows one theme's text on the other theme's background. Two more rules keep each theme consistent. First, the artifact is composited over a background the viewer paints in *its own* theme, so `body` must set an explicit `background` from a token; a transparent body shows the host's background with no warning. Second, every element that sets a color takes it from the same token set as the surface behind it, never from a literal that works in only one theme. Declare every token in the bare `:root` block before any media or `[data-theme]` block redefines it; a color that exists only inside one of those blocks is the classic unreadable-artifact bug. Give the second theme the same care as the first: don't simply invert it; keep contrast legible and keep the accent working on both backgrounds. A design that deliberately commits to one visual world (a neon arcade screen, a letterpress invitation) may stay single-theme: then omit the media query and `[data-theme]` blocks entirely but still set the background and every color explicitly, so the page looks right on either host background; do this by choice, never by omission.

**Use layout for spacing.** Lay out sibling groups with flex or grid and `gap` instead of per-element margins, which collapse or double without warning. Keep a side gutter of at least 16px at every width: set it once as side padding on `body` or one outer wrapper, whose vertical padding uses `padding-block` and never a `padding` shorthand that zeroes the sides. Let rows wrap or stack to one column at phone width (about 400px). Give images and any `aspect-ratio` box `max-width: 100%`, and don't give anything a `min-width` wider than the screen. Only wide tables, code, and diagrams may exceed it; give each `overflow-x: auto` on its own container so the page body never scrolls sideways. The publish skeleton pads `:root` top and bottom by the phone's safe-area insets (zero everywhere except a phone app) so the page runs edge to edge while its content stays clear of the system bars; keep that padding. A bar fixed to the top or bottom stays at `0` and adds `env(safe-area-inset-top, 0px)` or `env(safe-area-inset-bottom, 0px)` to its own padding. A sticky page header uses `top: env(safe-area-inset-top, 0px)` and never `0`. Size a one-screen app with `height: 100%` on `html` and `body` instead of `100vh`, so it fits inside that padding. A page that includes its own viewport meta gets this padding only when that meta declares `viewport-fit=cover`. Use `font-variant-numeric: tabular-nums` wherever digits line up in columns.

**Make repeated elements consistent.** For cards in a row, label/value pairs down a list, or badges on sibling items, use the same edges, baselines, and inner padding on each, and put any recurring element in the same place on each. Let content set a container's height and pick a column count the items fill, so nothing stretches over empty space or sits alone in a row. Make text that can outgrow its track wrap or scroll in its own container; clipped text is a bug.

**Use card styling selectively.** Border, fill, radius, and shadow each mark an element as a separate object. Apply them by role, to set off the one element that needs it; applying the same radius and shadow to every block flattens the hierarchy. Open with big-number tiles only when those figures are the point of the page.

**Draw charts to scale.** Place marks, ticks, and labels with one scale, and make every label name a value the chart actually reaches. Color chart text from the theme tokens so it is readable in both themes. Keep marks, labels, and edges clear of one another and inside the drawing's bounds; in SVG, leave room in the viewBox for the outermost labels and give every drawn shape an explicit fill.

**Make the page complete at rest.** Everything meant to be read is visible once the page has loaded, with no scrolling to trigger it; that first still frame is what a thumbnail, a shared link, and a skimming reader all see. A section may animate in, but from a visible resting state, never left at `opacity: 0` waiting for an observer. Size a hero to its content instead of to the viewport; a `100vh` opener pushes the rest of the page out of that first frame. A tool or app opens in a realistic working state: the user's real data where it exists, otherwise example rows, a loaded sample, or a plausibly filled form, clearly marked as examples and never presented as the user's own figures. The first view shows what the tool does; an empty shell waiting for input shows nothing. When those records live in the `db` capability, keep them out of the page source. Its first frame renders before the store answers, so make that frame a designed empty state that names what will appear and how to add the first entry, then fill it from the store. Seed the store through the `ArtifactData` tool (what type instructions call `write_db`) after the first publish: the user's real data, or marked examples for a tool only the user will use. For a store other people will fill with their own entries, seed only what the user gave you or asked for, never invented people or records.

**Avoid AI-generated design.** AI-generated design currently clusters around a few looks: warm cream (#F4F1EA) with a serif display and terracotta accent; near-black with a lone acid-green or vermilion pop; broadsheet hairline rules with dense columns; a purple-to-blue gradient hero on white; Inter or Space Grotesk as the "safe" face; emoji as section markers; everything centered; `rounded-lg` everywhere; accent bar/rail on rounded cards. When the user specifies a visual direction, follow it exactly; their words always win, including when they ask for one of these looks. When nothing is specified, don't use that freedom on one of these defaults.

**Build cleanly.** Watch for overlapping elements, cascade collisions, and silent font fallbacks. Close every non-void element, double-quote attributes, give keyboard focus a visible state, and respect `prefers-reduced-motion`. Give every form control a stable `id` (the platform preserves form values, focus, and scroll position across a republish). For generative or decorative graphics, use Canvas or WebGL instead of hand-writing long SVG path data.

**CSS rules.** When writing the CSS, watch your selector specificity. It is easy to generate classes that cancel each other out, e.g. a type-based selector like `.section` and an element-based one like `.cta` both setting padding and margins between sections. Structure the cascade so it doesn't undo your spacing unnoticed.

**Writing the copy.** Treat words as design material and never as decoration. Write from the user's side of the screen: name things by what people recognize instead of how the system is built (a person manages *notifications*; they don't manage *webhook config*). Use active voice; a control states exactly what happens ("Publish", then a toast that says "Published"). Errors explain what went wrong and how to fix it, without apologies or vagueness. Prefer specific to clever. Write plainly, the way a knowledgeable person would talk. Avoid mannered devices: asides set off by em-dashes, "not X, but Y" framing, colon-then-reveal sentences, scare quotes around invented labels, and stock phrases such as "worth noting" or "honest caveat". Prefer short, direct sentences over compressed or clever phrasing.

**Name the page like a product; don't caption it.** The `<title>` is the artifact's name in the gallery and the browser tab, and it gives the reader a first impression of the care taken. Give the page a real name: a short noun phrase, typically two to four words, specific to the subject; or, for a page that exists to answer one question, that question itself, which then is the page's name. When the user already has a specific name for the thing, use that name for the title rather than coining a new one. Stop at the name; a title that adds its own explanation after a dash or colon reads as generated filler. The name must also identify the page among many: in the gallery it appears beside dozens of other artifacts, and a generic category label that could apply to any of them fails as a name just as an appended explanation does. When a candidate title combines the name with a generic word (a greeting, a category, a page-type label), keep the name; a trim that drops the identifying part and keeps the generic word produces a title that could apply to any page. This rule removes explanations and doesn't require brevity: a multi-word title that already reads as one specific name is finished, and shortening it further only makes it generic. Put the explanation in the one-sentence publish `description`; the gallery shows it directly under the title.

**Structure is information.** Structural devices (numbering, eyebrows, dividers, labels) should encode something true about the content instead of decorating it. Many generic designs use numbered markers (01 / 02 / 03), but those fit only if the content actually is a sequence, such as a real process or a typed timeline where the order is information the reader needs. Before adding numbered markers or similar devices, check that they actually make sense.

**When the page is a UI (dashboard, tool).** It is scanned and operated instead of read top to bottom, so the craft shifts from typography to information design. Put the summary before the detail. Encode state in form as well as in numbers (a pill, a chip, a severity stripe) so that whatever needs attention is visible at a glance. Semantic color (good / warning / critical) is separate from the accent hue and doesn't count as your accent. Give sparklines and charts the same care as type: an area fill, a faint grid, an emphasized endpoint. Interactive elements should look interactive.



## Process

Start from what the viewer should be able to do on the page, in addition to what they will read. If the page should take input, keep what people change for whoever opens it next, show live data, or ask Claude something, load the `artifact-capabilities` skill now and design around what it makes available to this user. A page that is only read doesn't need that.

Before writing the page, settle a short design plan (a compact token system) and write it into the file itself, as the `:root` block at the top of the page's `<style>`, rather than into your reply:
- **Color**: the palette as 4-6 named color tokens.
- **Type**: font tokens for 2+ roles: a characterful display face used with restraint, a complementary body face, and a utility face for captions or data if needed.
- **Layout**: the layout concept as a one-line comment above the tokens.

Then build the rest of the page from those tokens, deriving every color and type decision from them. The plan is working material, not part of the answer: unless the user asks about the design, one plain sentence on the direction is the most to say about it, with no hex values or font names.

**Write, check once, publish.** Before publishing you may look at the rendered page once, where this session offers a way: one `ArtifactCheck` preview (or the Artifact tool's own `action: "preview"` where there is no separate `ArtifactCheck` tool), or else one screenshot of the local file; if the session offers none of these, skip the look. The preview renders desktop and phone widths in light and dark and lists overflow, colors that ignore the theme, blocked loads and console errors, including a script that fails to parse, so nothing it covers needs a check of your own. The look is optional: if you take it, make one pass of edits for what it shows, without a second look; then publish. For a page that charts real numbers, take the look rather than skip it, and spend it on the chart. A page whose point is logic (dates, money, scoring, parsing) may get one more check before publishing: one run of a pure function on a sample input, or, where no preview ran, one syntax check of its script; nothing more. A page that declares `capabilities` takes the look rather than skipping it, then one functional pass after the first publish, because the preview cannot run that code: read back once what the page stores or serves (one read of its stored data or one read-only route call; where that read alone would prove nothing, as on an empty store, you may first write one probe document yourself and delete it after the read, passing the `version` the write returned as `if_version`; no other test writes unless the user wants one), tell the user in one line what you exercised and what you could not, and stop. None of this becomes a loop, because the user is waiting for a link: no second screenshot, no scripts that probe the DOM, no re-running a check that passed. Review happens on the live page, and further polish is for the user to request; if the user reports something visibly broken (a clipped column, unreadable text, a control that does nothing), fix that, take at most one more look if the session offers a way, and republish once. These checks are for code you wrote into this page, not for content you fill into an Artifact made from an Artifact type (a Slides deck, a Design canvas): there the type's own instructions say whether to check, and if they say nothing, don't.

**Open viewers.** You don't need to do anything for viewers who already have the page open: published changes are delivered to them automatically at their next quiet moment, with state preserved where possible. If your page has state a viewer would miss (a game, a long form), register `window.claude?.hot?.snapshot(...)` and boot through `window.claude?.hot?.ready ? window.claude.hot.ready(start) : start(window.claude?.hot?.data ?? {})`; `hot` is the viewer's own update hook, not a capability behind `claude.use()`, and is absent outside a viewer, hence the `?.`.

## When the request is editorial

The stance changes here: the client has already rejected proposals that felt templated, and is paying for a distinctive point of view. Make opinionated decisions, and take one real aesthetic risk where it serves the work.

Review the design plan against the subject before building: if any part of it reads like the generic default you would produce for any similar page, revise that part in the plan itself, without narrating the revision to the user. Write the code only after the plan is specific to this subject, following the revised plan exactly.

**Principles** 

- The hero states the thesis: open with the most characteristic thing in the subject's world (headline, image, live demo, interactive moment). 
- Typography sets the personality of the page. Pair the display and body faces deliberately, avoiding the families you would use on any other project, and set a clear type scale with intentional weights, widths, and spacing. Make the type treatment itself a memorable part of the design instead of a neutral container for the content. 
- Use motion deliberately. Think about whether and where animation can serve the subject: a page-load sequence, hover micro-interactions, ambient atmosphere. One orchestrated moment is usually more effective than scattered effects; choose what the direction calls for. However, sometimes less is more, and extra animation adds to the impression that the design is AI-generated. 
- Match complexity to the vision. Maximalist directions need elaborate execution; minimal directions need precision in spacing, type, and detail. Elegance is executing the chosen vision well.
- Put your boldness in one place; keep everything around it quiet. If the accent clashes with the background, shift it toward an analogous hue or desaturate it instead of replacing it.

| Case | Before → after | Main cause | Component |
|---|---|---|---|

| P05 RFQ, 3 bidders | .415 → .566 | We replied one supplier at a time and took 72–95 s against the 60 s limit, so 4 of 8 sends timed out; one timeout pushed the most eager bidder to `final_offer` | transport / play loop |
| P08 raw material | .427 → .454 | Our concession froze (gap measured against a no-index price the supplier had refused), we resent the same sheets, and it went final in round 3 | bids, space |
| P10 capacity | .453 → .539 | We asked for 42 days against its 54 and treated that as free to the supplier; it charged about €7.4k of cost per day while the delay costs us €2.4k per day; it went final in round 1 | economics, plus an 82% anchor |
| P11 quality | .231 → **.147** | The supplier offered **€46.50 / 300 ppm / €150 chargeback** as an alternative sheet (would have scored .550) and we never saw it; we then asked for chargeback 500 again and lowered our own price | agent wiring, economics, bids |
| P18 raw material | .386 → .386 | Same freeze as P08; the 5% deadband compromise was filtered out | bids, space |

**Problems that affect many cases:**
1. **We never read the supplier's alternative sheets.** [agent.py:81-88](starter-kit/arena_kit/buyer/agent.py#L81-L88) reads only `term_sheets[0]`. 28 of 99 supplier messages carried an alternative, in 9 of 10 cases.
2. **Concessions freeze when the supplier insists on a term we price away.** The half-gap cap in [acceptance.py:159](starter-kit/arena_kit/buyer/acceptance.py#L159) measures the gap against terms the supplier has refused. This hit P08 and P18, and suppliers then go final early.
3. **Our model assumes the supplier gives up shorter lead times, chargebacks and similar terms for free.** It lacks lead-time and defect costs, so we ask for things the supplier charges us for (P10, P11).
4. **RFQ replies are sent one at a time, so threads time out** (P05).
5. **Smaller issues:**
   - We send identical sheets again.
   - The writer repeats questions the supplier has answered.
   - The writer thanks the supplier for reports it never attached.
   - We cite a complaint after the scorecard, and the arena marks it as a duplicate.

**Next:** after the synthesis and skeptic finish, I'll publish the status report as a shareable page: run history, code state, architecture, these findings and the ranked fixes. Then I'll implement the fixes that hold up and check them in the local simulator before you spend more quota.

The synthesis has finished, and the last stage, the skeptic, started at 17:03. It is checking each of the 8 ranked fixes against our best cases (P01, P03, P04, P07) and the simulator cases, to catch any fix that would make them worse. That usually takes 5–10 minutes. I haven't changed any code yet.

**What the synthesis concluded:** all of the losses came from our own code, not from bad supplier luck. Accepting and walking away worked correctly in every case. The ranked fixes, with estimated gains summed over the practice cases:

| # | Fix | Component | Est. gain | Cases |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | Read every term sheet the supplier sends, not only the first. If an alternative is cheaper, send it back as our offer so the supplier answers `agreed`, then accept | agent.observe, acceptance | +0.33 | P11, P18, P08, P05 |
| 2 | Account for what our asks cost the supplier: chargeback at its real defect rate, and a price for asking a faster lead time than it quoted | economics | +0.20 | P11, P10 |
| 3 | Measure the gap to the supplier's offer using the terms it insists on (for example its index clause), so we never freeze or resend identical sheets | bids, acceptance | +0.14 | P08, P18, P05, P02 |
| 4 | Send RFQ replies to each bidder concurrently, so the 60 s limit isn't missed | play.py | +0.10 | P05 |
| 5 | Track our concessions in real euros, without the estimated relationship cost, for relationship goals | bids | +0.10 | P02, P10 |
| 6 | Never visibly step back: hold instead of withdrawing a concession, and never lower the highest price we have shown | bids | +0.08 | P11, P18 |
| 7 | Treat a wider index deadband as a smaller ask than removing the clause, and count the supplier's own alternatives as its terms | space | +0.05 | P08, P18 |
| 8 | In no-alternative relationship cases, start no lower than 88% of the supplier's opening price | bids | +0.05 | P10 |

The estimates overlap, so they are rough, but together they point to a best-of mean well above today's 59.

**Next:**
1. When the skeptic finishes, I'll publish the status report for your colleague as a page with run history, code state, architecture, per-case findings and the vetted fix list.
2. Then I'll implement the fixes that hold up, roughly in the order 1, 6, 3, 2, 7, 5, 8, 4. Fix 4 (concurrency) is the riskiest change.
3. I'll check them in the local simulator, which uses no quota, before suggesting a targeted rerun.

There's one open question your colleague may be able to answer. The API says `accept` only takes the standing sheet, so accepting an alternative's id directly would probably be rejected as invalid (a 422). My plan sends the alternative back instead, which costs one round. Testing it on the free sandbox would settle it, but I'd need your go-ahead to do that.

Confirmed: the team's best-of mean is **65.3** across all 64 practice sessions. The difference from my 59.3 is that 3 of the 10 best scores came from sessions that weren't run with our buyer. They aren't in our `runs/` folder, so someone else on the team (your colleague?) is running a different agent with the same key:

| Case | Team best | Our buyer's best | Where the team best came from |
|---|---|---|---|
| P01 | **.932** | .810 | session at 16:38 (and .919 at 16:51) |
| P10 | **.625** | .539 | a 10-case run at 16:51 |
| P11 | **.620** | .147 / .231 | the same 16:51 run |
| others | — | ours is the best | — |

That 16:51 run averaged about 50. It beat us on P01, P10 and P11 and was worse everywhere else (P02 .087, P18 .166, P08 .218). Combining the two approaches is the opportunity.

**Quota:** 64 of 200 used, 136 left. The 16:51 run spent 10 of them, which wasn't in my count.

Their P11 session is the most useful result so far. It confirms fix #2 from the synthesis:
- **What they did:** offered 1500 ppm with **chargeback €0** and moved up in small steps (43.68 → 44.75).
- **How the supplier responded:** came down each round, 47 → 46.50 → 46 → 45.50, and closed at 45.50 (score .620).
- **What we did:** kept asking for chargeback €500, which this supplier prices at about €2.50 per unit, and ended at €49.
- **Conclusion:** a chargeback is expensive to the supplier, and our model treats it as free.

The supplier also kept saying "you have to give us faster payment terms" to them as well. That's a constant of this supplier.

**Next:**
- The skeptic stage is still running.
- I'll add their P01 (.932), P10 (.625) and P11 (.620) transcripts to the status report, as a "what worked elsewhere" section next to our forensics.
- If you can tell me who ran them and which code or branch they used, I'll compare the approaches directly instead of only from the transcripts.

"""EconomicEvaluator: the one place the buyer turns terms into euros. Normal moves, fallbacks and
acceptance all price through it, on the published cost function (`cost.total_cost`) with each
supplier's own standard terms. Supplier economics are estimates: the relationship term is priced
in three scenarios (low / mid / high C), never as a fact."""

import math

from ..cost import RELATIONSHIP_GOALS, closing_terms, supplier_value, total_cost
from .records import CandidatePackage, EvaluatedPackage, SupplierEstimate

SCENARIO = {"low": 0, "mid": 1, "high": 2}  # index into SupplierEstimate.full_cost; high = dearest C


def estimate_supplier(dossier, sid, price, cash_pressure=False, cap=None):
    """Full cost from the supplier's should-cost row, else the generic one, else 92 % of its price
    (the should-cost error of 5-15 % sets the spread). Cash pressure raises its cost of money.
    `cap`: the most its full cost can be - what its own cheapest sheet is worth to it less the
    sustainable margin (case P02: a should-cost above the ask made the relationship term cancel
    our price signal)."""
    found = (dossier.should_cost.get(sid) or dossier.should_cost.get("*")) if dossier else None
    if found:
        cost, conf = found
        spread, source = max(conf, 5.0) / 100, "should-cost"
    else:
        cost, spread, source = 0.92 * price, 0.07, "default"
    if cap is not None and 0 < cap < cost:
        cost = cap
    return SupplierEstimate(
        full_cost=(cost * (1 - spread), cost, cost * (1 + spread)),
        interest_rate=0.12 if cash_pressure else 0.08,
        source=source,
    )


class EconomicEvaluator:
    def __init__(self, case, std=None, estimates=None):
        self.case = case
        self.std = std or {}  # sid -> standard terms from its quote PDFs
        self.estimates = estimates or {}  # sid -> SupplierEstimate
        self.relationship = case["buyer"].get("category_goal") in RELATIONSHIP_GOALS and bool(self.estimates)

    def standard(self, sid):
        """The supplier's standard terms, completed from the case, as `cost.supplier_value` reads them."""
        return closing_terms(self.case, {"unit_price": 0.0}, self.std.get(sid))

    def supplier(self, sid, scenario="mid"):
        """Our estimate of the supplier for the relationship term; scenario "none" leaves it out."""
        est = self.estimates.get(sid)
        if not self.relationship or est is None or scenario == "none":
            return None
        return {
            "standard": self.standard(sid),
            "full_cost": est.full_cost[SCENARIO[scenario]],
            "interest_rate": est.interest_rate,
        }

    def c(self, sid, terms, scenario="mid"):
        return total_cost(self.case, terms, self.std.get(sid), self.supplier(sid, scenario))

    def c_alt(self):
        """C of the alternative; infinite without one (`kind: none`, or terms without a price)."""
        alt = self.case["buyer"].get("alternative") or {}
        terms = alt.get("terms") or {}
        return total_cost(self.case, terms) if terms.get("unit_price") else math.inf

    def cash_theirs(self, sid, terms):
        est = self.estimates.get(sid)
        supplier = {"standard": self.standard(sid), "interest_rate": est.interest_rate if est else 0.08}
        return supplier_value(self.case, terms, supplier)

    def evaluate(self, pkg: CandidatePackage) -> EvaluatedPackage:
        return EvaluatedPackage(
            pkg=pkg,
            c=self.c(pkg.sid, pkg.terms),
            c_high=self.c(pkg.sid, pkg.terms, "high"),
            cash_theirs=self.cash_theirs(pkg.sid, pkg.terms),
        )

    def best_price(self, sid, terms):
        """The price below which C rises again (relationship goals: squeezing costs); 0 without."""
        if self.supplier(sid) is None:
            return 0.0
        lo, hi = 0.3 * terms["unit_price"], 1.5 * terms["unit_price"]
        for _ in range(60):  # golden section: C is convex in the price
            a, b = lo + (hi - lo) * 0.382, lo + (hi - lo) * 0.618
            if self.c(sid, {**terms, "unit_price": a}) <= self.c(sid, {**terms, "unit_price": b}):
                hi = b
            else:
                lo = a
        return math.ceil((lo + hi) / 2 * 100) / 100

    def price_for(self, sid, terms, target_c):
        """The highest price in cents at which `terms` costs at most `target_c` (+1 cent: C is rounded),
        not below `best_price`; None if even that price costs more."""
        floor = self.best_price(sid, terms)
        p0 = max(terms["unit_price"], floor + 1.0)
        c0, c1 = self.c(sid, {**terms, "unit_price": p0}), self.c(sid, {**terms, "unit_price": p0 + 1})
        if c1 - c0 <= 0:
            return None
        if not floor:  # no relationship term: C is linear in the price
            p = p0 + (target_c - c0) / (c1 - c0)
        else:  # increasing above best_price: bisect
            lo, hi = floor, p0
            while self.c(sid, {**terms, "unit_price": hi}) < target_c:
                hi *= 1.5
            for _ in range(60):
                mid = (lo + hi) / 2
                lo, hi = (mid, hi) if self.c(sid, {**terms, "unit_price": mid}) <= target_c else (lo, mid)
            p = lo
        p = round(p, 2)
        for _ in range(3):  # the nearest cent, else the cents below it, until C fits
            if self.c(sid, {**terms, "unit_price": p}) <= target_c + 0.01:
                return p if p > 0 and p >= floor else None
            p = round(p - 0.01, 2)
        return None

That made assess flag R2 as a regression (773,217 -> 803,586), so bids.next_bid retracted to 697k and the bot answered 'you actually went backwards'. Three parts of the proposal are refuted or unsafe as written. (1) Switching standing/offer_id to the cheapest sheet uses an epsilon that is only 4 EUR in P01 run1, so a 61 EUR alternative (137.20 with effective date 2027-01-01) would become standing. That moves their_price, the select ceiling (it would drop 139.25/90) and the ours_at_theirs gap in our best case. In P07 R2 the margin is 288 against epsilon 336. (2) A min over the current message alone flags a false regression in the next round whenever an alternative disappears: P11 R3 has no alternative, so 765,267 -> 803,586 just moves the retraction one round later. (3) 'Send back an earlier alternative after a final_offer' has no EV gate, yet walk risk is real (api.md: 'push further and it may walk'). In P18 the gain is 2,390 against 33.9k of loss if it walks (P18's alternative is dearer than the opening, so a walk scores 0). Break-even walk probability is 6.6%. With the existing mirror gate (p_walk 0.35), the P11 send-back after the final also fails (24.9k < 31.8k), so the claimed P11 gain of about 0.33 is not reachable safely. Some evidence makes a send-back plausible: P05 bots that were pushed after a final_offer twice did not walk. Accepting by an '-a' id is undocumented. The P07 'agreed' message echoes its -4-a alternative, so the agreed branch must keep using the main id. The proposed unit test ('decide() returns a send with the -a terms' at R2) contradicts the decide logic: at R2 c_now 765k is far above next_c of about 730k. There are no alternatives in arena-sim, so the sim cases are unaffected.
   AMENDED: agent.observe: keep offer_id/standing = term_sheets[0] (bidding, ceiling, ours_at_theirs and generate stay on the main sheet). Add t.sheets = [(id, terms, c_none, valid_until_day)] for every priced sheet in every supplier message. A sheet stays valid while the cumulative reply_delay_days are within its validity_days; None means valid only in its own message. their_c[i] = min C over the feasible sheets valid at message i (this is a running min), so a dropped alternative is not a regression. Add t.best_alt = the valid feasible sheet with the lowest C when it beats the main sheet by more than max(epsilon, FIRM_STEP*C). acceptance.decide: (a) 'agreed' always accepts term_sheets[0].term_sheet_id. (b) closing()/urgent/cap-near/moves_left<=1 always accept the main id and never send. (c) When the open-thread accept test passes on best_alt (c_alt_sheet <= next_c+eps or time_up), not late, and moves_left>1, send best_alt.terms as our only sheet (reason 'take its alternative'). (d) For a final_offer: send best_alt back only if (1-p)*(c_now - c_best_alt) > p*max(0, fallback - c_now) with p = max(pb.p_walk, walk_threat risk), the same gate as mirror; otherwise accept the main sheet. Tests: P11 msg4 replay gives their_c[-1]=765,267, regressed False and no retraction; P11 msg6 is not regressed; P01 run1 and P07 replays send exactly the same packages as HEAD.

That implies about 5,700-7,100 ppm, which matches the proposed max(scorecard 2376, opening 6400) = 6400. To us the same switch is worth only 0.53 EUR/unit (8.3k). Insisting on cb 500 in every round R2-R5 was the main cost driver in P11. The change touches only cases with a chargeback lever (P11/P12/S08); P01/P03/P04/P07 have no chargeback lever, so it is a no-op there. Keeping the standing combo in select is low risk: in P01/P03/P04/P07 it already equals by_price[0]. Part (b) is refuted as written. The text says 'C for us is unchanged', but it also routes 'extra' into supplier(), and supplier() feeds relationship_cost, which changes our C, best_price and targets in P06/P09/P10. The claim that 56-day sheets get generated depends on exactly that C change: in the P10 replay, price_for returns None for 56 days because best_price is 26.32. With 'extra' in cash_theirs only, nothing new is generated. The lead premium itself is supported: the P10 bot cited a 'necessary price premium' for faster lead, and 35d cost +1.1 EUR vs 42d.

Tacto Negotiation Arena · buyer for Hollerau Pumpenwerke

Status report: practice runs, code state and the next fixes

As of Sat 10 Oct 2026, 17:25 Branch buyer-agent @ 1637ae8 (local, not pushed) Hosted runs made at f711dac Code freeze Sun 11 Oct, 12:00

This is a review request. It covers what the buyer is, how the last hosted practice round went and why, what I changed since, and the open questions where an experienced eye helps most. The questions are in section 8.

1. Summary

The buyer is a typed Python controller. Deterministic code decides every number, every accept and every walk-away. An LLM (gpt-6.1-sol, medium reasoning) only writes the e-mail text, and a guard checks every message before it is sent.

The last hosted round (6 cases) raised four scores and lowered one. A per-case forensic review found that every euro lost came from our own code, not from supplier luck. Acceptance and the guard behaved correctly in every case. The losses trace to four mechanisms:

  1. We ignored the supplier's alternative term sheets. The agent read only the first sheet of each supplier message, and 28 of 99 supplier messages carried a second one. In P11 an ignored alternative would have scored 0.550; we closed at 0.147.
  2. Our concessions froze or overshot. The gap was measured against terms the supplier had refused, so we resent identical sheets and it went final (P08, P18). In relationship cases, a small C step near our estimated floor became a large price jump (P02).
  3. We treated our asks as free to the supplier. A €500 chargeback and a faster delivery cost the supplier money, and it charged us for them in the price (P11, P10).
  4. RFQ replies are sent one supplier at a time. With 3 bidders our replies took 72–95 s against the 60 s limit, so 4 of 8 sends timed out (P05).

Items 1, 2 (partly) and 3 (partly) are fixed and committed locally. Hosted suppliers go final after our 3rd to 5th message, so the concession plan now spans 5 messages instead of 6–9. That lifted the local persona simulator from 0.545 to 0.570. Nothing new has been validated on the hosted arena yet.

2. Where we stand

Score per case is clip((C_open − C_deal) / (C_open − C_best), 0, 1). Practice keeps the best session per case. The "team best" column includes sessions run by another agent on our key (see section 7).

4. The last hosted round, case by case

Six cases rerun at commit f711dac, 16:44–16:47. Each was reviewed by reconstructing every round, pricing every supplier sheet with our cost function, reading the supplier's stated reasons and tracing each mistake to code. A separate skeptic pass then tried to refute each finding against our best cases.

P11 · quality 0.231 → 0.147 agent wiring, economics, bids

What happened
Round 1 went well: the supplier took our 300 ppm / €150 chargeback terms at €47.00. In round 2 every sheet we sent asked for a €500 chargeback again. The supplier priced that at +€2.00–2.50 per unit (€49.00) and attached an alternative at €46.50 / 300 ppm / €150. We never saw the alternative. Its dearer standing sheet looked like a regression, so we lowered our own price from €44.53 to €42.30. The supplier replied "you actually went backwards on the price", held €49.00 and went final in round 5.
Missed
The ignored alternative: C 765,267, score 0.550, about €38k better than the deal.
Root cause
The agent read only term_sheets[0]. The supplier-value model used 0 ppm when the quote had no standard ppm, so a chargeback looked free to the supplier. A "regression" withdrew our last concession.

P18 · raw material 0.386 → 0.386 bids, space

What happened
The supplier said three times that a fixed price over 24 months was impossible and the AS-14404 index clause was mandatory. We measured the gap to its price on our no-clause terms, which was already below our own bid, so our concession was zero. In round 3 we resent identical sheets, and it went final at 5.50 with a 0% deadband.
Missed
The compromise it offered twice itself, a 5% deadband: about 5.50 / 60 d / 5% at C 263,046, score about 0.44 (+€4–6k).
Root cause
The half-gap cap was measured on a structure the supplier had refused. The space treated any index-clause change as a full ask, so 5% deadband sheets were filtered out as dominated.

P08 · raw material 0.427 → 0.454 bids, space

What happened
The same mechanism as P18. After a large supplier move we conceded +€942, then exactly 0, resent identical sheets, and it went final in round 3 of 10. We only ever offered 0% deadband clauses, the costliest for us.
Missed
Its 90-day payment term at the final price: about +0.04.

P02 · price increase 0.358 → 0.488 bids

What happened
In round 2 we answered a €1.28 per unit supplier step with a +€4.03 jump. Reciprocity is measured in our C, which includes our estimate of the relationship cost. Near that estimated floor C is almost flat in price, so a small C step becomes a large price step. The supplier then moved only €0.6–1.2 per round and went final in round 4 at €372.05.
Missed
About €7.5k on a reciprocal path (about +0.15). Accepting the final was correct.

P10 · capacity, no alternative 0.453 → 0.539 economics

What happened
We asked for 42 days against its quoted 54. The supplier charged about €0.16 per unit per day for faster delivery, about €7.4k of C per day, against our late cost of €2.4k per day. It went final in round 1 at €34.00. A slower 56-day sheet was never generated.
Missed
About 56 d at €31.80–32.20: +0.085 to +0.116.

P05 · RFQ, 3 bidders 0.415 → 0.566 transport

What happened
The new market anchor (f711dac) lifted the score. But the play loop serves one thread at a time: a full round took 73–111 s against the 60 s limit, and 4 of 8 sends timed out. One timeout turned the hungriest bidder, which had just dropped €7.50 in one step, into a final offer at €31.00. About 21 s went by before our first send, on labels for every thread plus the writer. Held threads received identical sheets ("can't negotiate against myself").
Missed
About +0.06 to +0.11 if replies were on time.

When suppliers go final

Across all 17 of our hosted sessions, every supplier went final after our 3rd to 5th message (P10 after the 1st). Our concession plan spanned 6–9 messages, so by the final we had used only about 5–10% of our room. This is why the plan now spans 5 messages.

8. Questions for review

  1. The other agent. Who runs it, and can we see its code? Combining what worked (P01, P10, P11) with our buyer looks like the quickest gain.
  2. Accepting an alternative. The API says accept takes the supplier's standing sheet, and an unknown id is a 422. We send the alternative back as our sheet instead, which costs one round. Is a sandbox test of accepting an -a id worth it?
  3. Concession pace. Suppliers go final after message 3–5. Is the final triggered by a round count or by our behaviour (identical sheets, small moves)? If by round count, conceding faster is right. If by behaviour, holding firm costs us more than we thought.

content.text:
Written for: an experienced colleague reviewing the buyer agent and the practice results.

The status report is here: https://claude.ai/artifact/K6ERsc52i72RbyD9JjdnRN

It's private. Your colleague can open it only after you share it from the page's Share menu.

It covers the practice scores per case, how the buyer works (with a flow diagram), the last round case by case, the fix list, local simulator results, what the other agent did better, 7 questions for review, and the plan to Sunday.

**What changed since my last update:**
- **Skeptic:** it kept 7 of the 8 fixes, with amendments, and dropped the anchor bound (fix 8).
- **Two local commits on `buyer-agent`, not pushed:**
  - `aea7c52` makes four changes:
    - reads every supplier sheet and sends a cheaper alternative back;
    - holds instead of stepping back;
    - unfreezes the gap measurement;
    - makes chargeback and faster delivery cost the supplier when we rank sheets.
  - `1637ae8` applies the skeptic's amendments and plans concessions over 5 messages instead of 6–9.
- **Local results:**
  - Persona simulator: 0.545 → **0.570**, now above naive's 0.560.
  - Scripted simulator: 0.797 → 0.790, a small expected cost.
  - All 135 tests pass.
- **Not yet checked on the hosted arena.**

**Decisions for you:**
1. **Push?** Your colleague can't see the new code until `buyer-agent` is pushed; origin is still at 624a93f. Do you want me to push it?
2. **The other agent:** who runs it, and where is its code? Its P11 session (chargeback €0, small steps, scored .620) shows exactly what our fix 2 aims for, and it beat us on P01 and P10 too.
3. **Hosted rerun:** once fixes 3, 5 and 7 are finished, I'd suggest rerunning P02, P08, P10, P11 and P18 from a frozen copy at the new commit. That costs 5 sessions of the 136 left.

I'll continue with fixes 3, 5 and 7 now.

This session is being continued from a previous conversation that ran out of context. The summary below covers the earlier portion of the conversation.

Summary:
1. Primary Request and Intent:
   - **Context.** The Tacto Negotiation Arena hackathon: a buyer agent for Hollerau Pumpenwerke, scored on total cost.
     - Live Final and code freeze: Sun 11 Oct 2026, 12:00.
     - Submission on ehl.gg: repo, README with env var names, the exact commit hash, approach description and slides.
     - Today is Sat 10 Oct 2026, about 17:25.
   - **Main approved plan:** /Users/osama.salem/.claude/plans/memoized-meandering-acorn.md. A typed deterministic-core buyer with LLM phrasing, validated in the simulator, with deliverables BUYER.md, README and an evaluation report.
   - **Recent user requests, in order:**
     - "how to run all cases?" (answered with the 10-case command from the frozen copy ehl-run).
     - "Could you walk through the last round of negotiations, the responses, the history and refine the submissions, understand what went wrong and which agent caused the issue."
     - "Ok can you make an extensive status report of the previous runs the code state so my experienced colleague can give you feedback?" This is a document for someone else, so it was published as an Artifact.
     - Status checks: "What is the current status?", "what is going on now?", "is the skeptic done?"
     - "btw we are 65 now 59": the team leaderboard best-of is 65.3, not 59.
   - **Standing constraints (keep these):**
     - Never print or commit .env values.
     - Never push `entire/*` branches; they hold keys.
     - Work on the `buyer-agent` branch, never main.
     - Do not push without the user's approval.
     - Mind the quota and state the session cost of every suggested run.
     - The user starts hosted practice runs; the classifier blocks me. Read-only GETs on our own sessions are fine.
     - The final runner must not call /v1/events*, /screen, /leaderboard, /results or their JSON variants.
     - No smoke tests, no bloat, lean code (CLAUDE.md).

2. Key Technical Concepts:
   - **Score and outcomes:**
     - Score = clip((C_open − C_deal)/(C_open − C_best), 0, 1). Practice keeps the best session per case.
     - A broken must-have scores 0. No deal scores the alternative, which is 0 if none.
   - **API rules:**
     - `accept` takes the supplier's standing term sheet (api.md:95). An unknown or stale id is a 422, so an alternative "-a" sheet must be sent back as our only sheet; the supplier then answers `agreed`.
     - Supplier messages often carry alternative term_sheets: 28 of 99 supplier messages, in 9 of 10 cases.
     - `final_offer`: pushing may make the supplier walk.
   - **Supplier behaviour:** hosted suppliers go final after our 3rd–5th message (P10 after the 1st).
   - **Relationship goals** (stabilise, secure_supply): C includes an estimated relationship cost. Near that floor, C is flat in price, so small C steps become big price jumps (P02).
   - **`cost.supplier_value`** uses `ppm` (default: the std ppm, else 0) and `extra`. Contract length and the index clause do not count.
   - **Quota:** 64 of 200 sessions used, 136 left. The other agent on the same key used about 20+ of them, including a 10-case run at 16:51 that averaged about 50.
   - **Timing:**
     - LLM turn call p50 9.2 s, p90 12.8 s. Decision per turn p50 9.3 s, p90 22.2 s.
     - Writer source: 55 llm, 7 template.

3. Files and Code Sections (all under /Users/osama.salem/Documents/ehl/starter-kit):
   - **`arena_kit/buyer/records.py`**: added to `SupplierThreadState`:
     ```python
     sheets: list[dict] = field(default_factory=list)  # every priced sheet of its last message, standing first
     my_sheets: list[dict] = field(default_factory=list)  # the sheets of our last message
     ```
   - **`arena_kit/buyer/agent.py`**:
     - Imports `from ..cost import must_haves_ok`.
     - `observe()` builds `EconomicEvaluator(case, std, estimates, {sid: _quoted(ev, std[sid]) for sid, ev in threads.items()})`.
     - The state now has `their_c=[_c_msg(econ, case, sid, m, std[sid]) for m in theirs]`, `sheets=[s["terms"] for s in sheets if (s.get("terms") or {}).get("unit_price") is not None]` and `my_sheets=[s["terms"] for s in mine[-1]["term_sheets"]] if mine else []`.
     - `offer_id` and `standing` stay at `term_sheets[0]`.
     - New helpers:
     ```python
     def _quoted(ev, std):
         sheets = [m["term_sheets"][0].get("terms") or {} for m in ev if m.get("from") != "buyer" and m.get("term_sheets")]
         first, last = (sheets[0], sheets[-1]) if sheets else ({}, {})
         return {"ppm": first.get("ppm_commitment") or std.get("ppm_commitment"),
                 "lead": last.get("lead_time_days") or std.get("lead_time_days")}

     def _c_msg(econ, case, sid, m, std):
         sheets = [s.get("terms") or {} for s in m["term_sheets"]]
         ok = [_c(econ, sid, s) for s in sheets if must_haves_ok(case, s, std)]
         return min(ok, default=_c(econ, sid, sheets[0]))
     ```
   - **`arena_kit/buyer/economics.py`**:
     - Added `LEAD_DAY = 0.003`.
     - `EconomicEvaluator.__init__(self, case, std=None, estimates=None, quoted=None)` sets `self.quoted`.
     - `cash_theirs` now sets `supplier["ppm"] = q["ppm"]` when that is higher than the std ppm, and `supplier["extra"] = -LEAD_DAY * terms["unit_price"] * max(0, q["lead"] - terms["lead_time_days"])`.
     - This affects only cash_theirs, i.e. ranking. `supplier()` and `best_price` are unchanged.
   - **`arena_kit/buyer/bids.py`**:
     - `next_bid` now does `if a.regressed or hold: return last` (hold instead of withdrawing).
     - Docstring updated. `select` is unchanged; the ceiling is still the supplier's price.
   - **`arena_kit/buyer/acceptance.py`**:
     - New `alternative(cs, ev, space, t, threads)`:
       - Returns None if `t.moves_left <= 1`.
       - For each sheet in `t.sheets[1:]`, completes `stated = {**std levers, **s}` via `space.complete(stated, t.std, partial(ev.c, t.sid))`.
       - Skips sheets that are invalid or already in `t.my_sheets`.
       - Requires `ev.c(..., "none") <= cs.c_alt` and `p.c_high <= floor_c` of the other threads.
       - Returns the cheapest sheet beating `c_now - epsilon`.
     - In `decide`:
       - `alt = None if late else alternative(...)`.
       - Final-offer branch: `p = max(pb.p_walk, walk_threat risk)`, `risk = p*max(0, fallback - c_now)`. The alternative is sent only if `(1-p)*(c_now-alt.c) > risk`; the mirror uses the same risk.
       - `c_best = min(c_now, alt.c)`.
       - Fix 3: `if t.my_c and ours_at_theirs <= t.my_c[-1] + eps: ours_at_theirs = c_best`.
       - Accept test: `if ready and (takeable or alt) and (c_best <= next_c + eps or time_up) and not (a.regressed and not time_up)`. If `alt`, it sends the alternative ("close: its own cheaper alternative").
       - Packages: `select(..., their_price)`, then filter with `_cut` (never the same terms at a lower price than we showed):
     ```python
     def _cut(terms, shown):
         same = all(terms[f] == shown.get(f) for f in terms if f != "unit_price")
         return same and terms["unit_price"] < shown.get("unit_price", 0)
     ```
   - **`arena_kit/buyer/playbook.py`**: GOALS max_rounds now 5 for every goal.
     ```python
     "leverage": (0.3, 0.5, 3, 5, 0.25, True, 25.0),
     "stabilise": (0.8, 0.9, 2, 5, 0.40, False, 25.0),
     "secure_supply": (1.0, 1.0, 1, 5, 0.50, False, 20.0),
     "quality_first": (0.5, 0.7, 2, 5, 0.35, True, 25.0),
     "routine": (0.6, 0.8, 1, 5, 0.30, True, 15.0),
     ```
     A backup of the old file is in scratchpad/playbook.bak.
   - **`tests/test_buyer_policy.py`**:
     - Renamed the old test to `test_a_regression_meets_a_hold_and_is_not_accepted_early`, which expects 199_000.
     - Added `test_its_own_cheaper_alternative_is_sent_back_not_its_dearer_final_offer_accepted`: final_offer with sheets [full@109, alt@104] sends the alternative; with `my_sheets=[alt]` it accepts.
     - 135 passed, 1 skipped; ruff clean.
   - **Commits on buyer-agent (local, not pushed):**
     - aea7c52 "Use every supplier sheet, hold instead of stepping back, unfreeze bids, price what our asks cost the supplier"
     - 1637ae8 "Plan concessions over 5 messages; gate an alternative after a final offer; no lower price on shown terms"
     - The hosted runs were made at f711dac in the frozen worktree /Users/osama.salem/Documents/ehl-run. origin/buyer-agent is at 624a93f.
   - **Scratchpad** (/private/tmp/claude-501/-Users-osama-salem-Documents-ehl/85659574-f9ad-4761-bdf5-07c4c69e9023/scratchpad):
     - `review/<case>_<sid>.json`: the full hosted dumps.
     - `scores2.py`, `dumpall.py`.
     - `rp.py`: offline replay of a single-supplier transcript through the current core. Usage: `uv run python $SP/rp.py P11_50bb682473fc5c06.json`.
     - `status/buyer-status.html`: the report.
     - Workflow output: `tasks/w7emva3b2.output` (reviews, synthesis, skeptic).

4. Errors and fixes:
   - **Expected test failure:** the regression test expected the old retraction; updated it to expect a hold.
   - **Ruff E501 line too long** in acceptance.py: split into the `stated` variable, and simplified the late check to `alt = None if late else ...`.
   - **zsh `echo ======`** caused "===== not found"; ran the evals separately.
   - **The first alternative-counting script** counted buyer messages; refiltered to supplier messages only (from `sales@`).
   - **Skeptic refutations, applied:**
     - Reverted the shown-price ceiling (fix 6).
     - Added the EV gate for sending an alternative after a final offer (fix 1).
     - No alternative when late.

5. Problem Solving:
   - **Forensic findings, verdicts:**
     - **P11** (.147): ignored alternative 46.50/300/150 (would score .550); cash_theirs used ppm 0, so chargeback 500 looked free; a regression withdrew our concession ("you went backwards").
     - **P18** (.386) and **P08** (.454): the half-gap measured on a refused no-clause structure froze our bids; identical sheets; final in round 3. Binary index_clause demand filtered out the 5% deadband.
     - **P02** (.488): reciprocity in relationship C overshot, +4.03 €/unit against the supplier's 1.28.
     - **P10** (.539): asked 42 d against its 54 d; the supplier charges about 0.157 €/unit/day; final in round 1.
     - **P05** (.566): the serial play loop caused 4 of 8 sends to time out.

   - **Offline replay:**

     - P11 now generates chargeback 0 sheets, matching the other agent's .620 path.
     - P18 still moves only a little (+327), because the supplier's real improvement, counting its alternative, was small.
     - P10 is unchanged: no 56 d sheet, because price_for falls below the relationship floor.
   - **Other agent's sessions** (not ours): P01 .932/.919, P10 .625, P11 .620. Their P11 run used 1500 ppm, chargeback 0 and small steps; the supplier went 47 → 45.50.

7. Pending Tasks:

"""Grounded supplier observations; fixed classifications first, rich interpretation only when useful."""

import hashlib
import json
import re
from dataclasses import asdict

from .model import parse_json
from .prompts import FIELDS, INTERPRET
from .records import SupplierObservation

MATERIAL = re.compile(
    r"\b(if|provided|conditional|unless|drawing|specification|approval|approve|dispute|incorrect|"
    r"confidential|breakdown|wenn|sofern|freigabe|zeichnung|intern|falsch)\b",
    re.I,
)
FINAL = re.compile(r"\b(final|last offer|cannot move|no further|endgültig|letztes angebot|mehr ist nicht drin)\b", re.I)
CASH = re.compile(r"\b(cash flow|liquidity|prepayment|faster payment|shorter payment|liquidität|vorkasse)\b", re.I)
FIELD_WORDS = {
    "payment_days": r"payment|prepayment|zahlung|vorkasse",
    "contract_months": r"contract|commitment|vertrag",
    "volume_per_year": r"volume|quantity|volumen|menge",
    "lead_time_days": r"lead time|capacity|lieferzeit|kapazität",
    "effective_date": r"effective|start date|wirksam",
    "ppm_commitment": r"ppm|quality|qualität",
}


def identity(sid, message):
    body = message.get("body") or ""
    mid = str(
        message.get("message_id")
        or message.get("id")
        or hashlib.sha256(json.dumps(message, sort_keys=True, default=str).encode()).hexdigest()[:16]
    )
    fingerprint = hashlib.sha256(f"{sid}\0{mid}\0{body}".encode()).hexdigest()
    return mid, fingerprint


def interpret(sid, message, *, model=None, decisions=None, budget_s=0, deadline=None, brief=None, asked=()):
    body = message.get("body") or ""
    mid, fingerprint = identity(sid, message)
    label = (
        decisions.classify_reply(body, timeout_s=min(3.0, max(0, budget_s))) if decisions and budget_s >= 3 else None
    )
    label = label or {}
    values = tuple(label.get("values") or [f for f, words in FIELD_WORDS.items() if re.search(words, body, re.I)])
    firmness = 3 if label.get("firm_final") or FINAL.search(body) else 1
    # These rules preserve business dependencies without promoting them to official offer status.
    dependencies = tuple(
        {"text": "Technical approval or specification remains unresolved.", "evidence": body[:300]}
        for _ in [0]
        if re.search(
            r"(?:requires?|pending|subject to|awaiting|need|benötig|vorbehalt).{0,80}"
            r"(?:drawing|specification|approval|freigabe|zeichnung)",
            body,
            re.I,
        )
    )
    refused = (
        ("breakdown",)
        if re.search(r"do not disclose|confidential|figures stay|keine.*kosten|intern", body, re.I)
        else ()
    )
    answered = (
        ("breakdown",) if re.search(r"attached.*breakdown|breakdown.*attached|cost breakdown.*sent", body, re.I) else ()
    )
    if "lead_time" in asked and re.search(r"(?:lead time|lieferzeit).{0,30}\d", body, re.I):
        answered += ("lead_time",)
    fallback = SupplierObservation(
        mid,
        fingerprint,
        intent=label.get("intent", "walk_threat" if firmness == 3 else "hold"),
        firmness=firmness,
        cash_pressure=bool(label.get("cash_pressure") or CASH.search(body)),
        values=values,
        dependencies=dependencies,
        answered=answered,
        refused=refused,
        source="decisions" if label else "rules",
    )
    if not model or budget_s < 15 or not MATERIAL.search(body):
        return fallback
    system, user = INTERPRET.render(
        case_id=sid,
        case_type="reply",
        goal="procurement",
        rev=0,
        budget_s=budget_s,
        brief=json.dumps(asdict(brief)) if brief else "(none)",
        message_id=mid,
        asked=json.dumps(list(asked)),
        reply=body[:6000],
    )

    def validate(raw):
        out = parse_json(raw)
        errors = INTERPRET.check(out)
        if errors:
            return errors
        evidence = [
            *out["evidence"],
            *(t["evidence"] for t in out["conditional_trades"]),
            *(t["evidence"] for t in out["dependencies"]),
        ]
        if not evidence or any(not e.strip() or e not in body for e in evidence):
            errors.append("observation requires verbatim reply evidence")
        if any(f not in FIELDS for f in out["values"]):
            errors.append("unknown field")
        if (out["answered"] or out["refused"]) and not out["evidence"]:
            errors.append("question status requires evidence")
        if set(out["answered"]) & set(out["refused"]):
            errors.append("question cannot be answered and refused together")
        return errors

    raw = model.complete(
        system,
        user,
        min(INTERPRET.budget_s, max(0, budget_s - 3)),
        role="interpretation",
        deadline=deadline,
        validate=validate,
    )
    out = parse_json(raw)
    if not out:
        return fallback
    return SupplierObservation(
        mid,
        fingerprint,
        intent=out["intent"],
        firmness=out["firmness"],
        cash_pressure=out["cash_pressure"],
        values=tuple(out["values"]),
        conditional_trades=tuple(out["conditional_trades"]),
        dependencies=tuple(out["dependencies"]),
        answered=tuple(out["answered"]),
        refused=tuple(out["refused"]),
        evidence=tuple(out["evidence"]),
        source="model",
    )

I read the other agent's unstaged changes (31 modified files, 6 new, about +2,260/−1,230 lines) and found no obvious bug, so I changed nothing. Tests (201 passed, 1 skipped) and ruff are clean.

I ran both local simulators on the working tree. The scripted simulator mean is 0.794, against 0.790 at my last commit. The persona simulator mean is 0.602. Neither comparison is like for like: S04 now comes back unscored, so those means cover 8 cases.

**What the changes are:** a large rework, not a bug fix.
- **Runner:** `play.py` gets a coordinator with authoritative clocks, optional parallel sends, and recovery of ambiguous sends.
- **Guard:** `guard.py` gets a financial check that applies to every move. It also makes all free prose number-free.
- **Interpreter:** a new `interpreter.py` reads each supplier reply and a persisted brief.
- **Scoring:** the simulator now checks claims, and its scoring can come back "unscored".
- **Economics:** the relationship cost now applies consistently, and supplier-specific cost evidence is no longer capped.

**Behaviour changes you should know about.** I left these alone because they are deliberate, with tests rewritten to match:

1. **Relationship cost in `feasible`:**
   - This reverses the P01 fix (624a93f). The test that guarded it now expects a walk instead of an accept.
   - A rough relationship estimate can again turn a final offer that beats the alternative into a walk-away.
   - P01 is our best case, so I'd want your colleague's view before the final.
2. **Unresolved dependencies:**
   - If a supplier's reply matches "requires/pending/subject to … approval/drawing/specification", the sheet is treated as unacceptable.
   - On a `final_offer`, nothing is sent and we walk away. The regex is loose ("need … approval").
   - A false match would lose a good final offer.
3. **Late close:** from 60% of the wave's time, we now close on the best feasible sheet even if the supplier is still moving.
4. **Price ceiling:** the supplier's own price no longer caps what we show, so our sheets can be dearer than its price. That undoes my earlier P02/P18 ceiling.
5. **S04 unscored:**
   - The simulator now sets `c_open` only from opening quotes that meet the must-haves. S04's opening doesn't, so S04 scores "n/a".
   - At my commit S04 scored 0.791, so this is a change in how the simulator scores, not in the buyer's play.

Nothing was committed or staged, and I removed the temporary comparison worktree I used.

**Decision for you:** do you want me to revert item 1, so a final offer that beats the alternative is never turned into a walk? It's a small change, but it undoes something the other agent did on purpose.
And thing worth updating? Then you can do it if you are sure

I made one fix, in the other agent's unstaged work, and left everything else alone. Tests (201 passed, 1 skipped) and ruff are clean. I did not re-run the simulators after the fix.

**What changed:** "can we take this sheet?" no longer includes the rough relationship-cost estimate again. Before, that estimate could push a final offer over the alternative and trigger a walk-away. That is the P01 bug fixed in 624a93f.

- **P01, .93:** the bid opened about 9% under the ask (126 against 138.55). Concessions were tiny, around 0.3–1.5 a round, over 6 rounds, with 3 payment/start-date variants at about the same cost. The supplier walked from 138.55 down to 135.7 by itself.
- **P11, .62:** 1500 ppm, chargeback 0, steps of about 0.3, over 7 rounds. The supplier went 47 → 45.5.
- **P10, .625:** the offer was 0.02 under the ask with the 56-day lead time, and was agreed in round 1.
- **P18, .52:** a price-and-payment mix, with an index clause at 0.45 share and 0 deadband.

The pattern is a low anchor, then long, small steps while the supplier keeps moving.

**Local checks on `5d5f4db`:**
- **Tests and lint:** 201 pass, ruff is clean.
- **Simulators:** scripted 0.790, persona 0.601.

**Open risk on P01:** our reservation is almost equal to our first bid, because the relationship-cost floor leaves little room. We will mostly hold, and the supplier then has to keep moving the way it did in the .93 run.

**Run prepared:** the frozen copy `ehl-run2` is at `5d5f4db`, and the key file is in place.

**Proposed run (you decide):** P01, P02, P11, P18 and P08, 5 sessions of the 111. I'd skip P03, P04 and P07, since they are already high, and skip P05 and P10 until we see these. I'd read the result from the leaderboard.
